mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent recessionary periods.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO drop > 2% does not correlate with subsequent supply chain issues.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and starts to rise, it signals the beginning of a tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS rising from < 1% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent economic expansions.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 jobs in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) simultaneously decreases, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition of PAYEMS and UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent strong labor markets.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is positive and retail sales (RSAFS) are also increasing, it signals robust consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth positive and RSAFS increasing
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition of GDPC1 and RSAFS does not correlate with subsequent periods of robust consumer demand.
